question: A developer wants Claude Code to update a deprecated log statement logger.warn("legacy-path") that appears twice in the same file, in two different functions, where only one of the two occurrences should change. Claude issues an Edit call with old_string set to exactly that log statement and the call fails. What is the correct next step?
options: A) Switch to Grep with the multiline flag to rewrite the matching line directly, since Grep can modify file contents once a match is found
B) Set replace_all to true on the same Edit call so both occurrences update identically, then manually revert whichever one should have stayed
C) Widen old_string to include enough surrounding context to uniquely identify the intended occurrence, then retry Edit with that string
D) Call Write with only the new log line as content, expecting Write to merge that single line into the correct spot in the existing file
correct_answers: C) Widen old_string to include enough surrounding context to uniquely identify the intended occurrence, then retry Edit with that string
explanations: Incorrect. Grep is read-only and searches file contents; it has no capability to write or modify files, so it cannot perform the edit.

Incorrect. replace_all rewrites every occurrence, which would also change the log statement the developer wants to keep, and reverting one afterward risks losing track of which change was intentional.

Correct. Edit requires old_string to match exactly once; when a string occurs more than once, supplying additional surrounding context that appears only around the target occurrence restores uniqueness and lets Edit apply cleanly.
Incorrect. Write overwrites the entire file with exactly the content provided; passing only a single line would delete the rest of the file's contents rather than merging into it.
